helm upgrade --install cert-manager jetstack/cert-manager -n cert-manager --create-namespace --version v1.18.2 --set crds.enabled=true

🌳 ClusterIssuer
① Which CA?group
spec.acme.serverstringrequiredACME directory URL
ValueMeaning
…acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directoryproduction (rate limited)
…acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directorystaging — untrusted certs, for testing

② How to prove?group

• spec.acme.solvers[].selectorobjectwhich names use this solver (dnsZones, dnsNames)

6.2Certificate — annotation vs explicit

In one sentence

Either let cert-manager create a Certificate from the Ingress annotation, or write the Certificate yourself when you need wildcards or shared names.

Two ways to ask for a certificate

Annotation on the IngressExplicit Certificate
Howcert-manager.io/cluster-issuer on an Ingress with spec.tlsa Certificate object
Namestaken from tls[].hostsdnsNames you list
Good forone Ingress = one certificatewildcards, shared certs, custom duration/key
Jahezapi-ingress, partners-ingresswildcard-jahez-net-certificate
📄 tls/wildcard-jahez-net-certificate.yamlyaml
# tls/wildcard-jahez-net-certificate.yaml — explicit Certificate (wildcard needs DNS-01)
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: wildcard-jahez-net-certificate
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which names?
  dnsNames:
    - menu.jahez.net
    - orders.jahez.net
    - "*.preview.jahez.net"
  # ② Who signs it?
  issuerRef:
    name: letsencrypt-prod-cluster-issuer
    kind: ClusterIssuer
  # ③ Where is it stored?
  secretName: wildcard-jahez-net-tls-secret
  # ④ When is it renewed?
  duration: 2160h       # 90 days (Let's Encrypt maximum)
  renewBefore: 720h     # renew 30 days before expiry
  privateKey:
    algorithm: ECDSA
    size: 256
    rotationPolicy: Always

🌳 Certificate
① Which names?group
• spec.dnsNameslistSANs; wildcards need DNS-01
② Who signs it?group
• spec.issuerRefobjectrequiredname + kind (Issuer / ClusterIssuer)
③ Where is it stored?group
• spec.secretNamestringrequiredTLS Secret name the Ingress uses
④ When renewed?group
• spec.durationstringrequested lifetime (LE caps at 90d)
• spec.renewBeforestringrenew this long before expiry
• spec.privateKey.rotationPolicystringAlways = new key on each renewal
✕ When it fails
  • Challenge stuck pending: HTTP-01 → DNS not at the NLB yet or :80 blocked; DNS-01 → IRSA lacks route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets.
  • Too many failed attempts → Let’s Encrypt rate limit; test with the staging issuer first.

7

Egress and NetworkPolicy

The other direction: who may talk to a Pod, and where a Pod may talk to.

7.0How a NetworkPolicy works

In one sentence

A NetworkPolicy selects Pods and turns the listed directions into allow-lists; everything not allowed by some policy is dropped.

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
① Which Pods does it protect?podSelectorwhich flats get a lock
② Which directions are locked?policyTypesfront door, back door or both
③ Who may come in?ingress[].from · portsguest list
④ Where may they go?egress[].to · portsallowed destinations
Familynetworking.k8s.io/v1
Scopenamespaced
Enforced byCNI (VPC CNI agent · Calico · Cilium)
Logicallow-lists, union of all policies
Short namenetpol
⎈ Full cluster · After Ingress — one NLB, ingress-nginx Pods route by host + path
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen
Lit: NetworkPolicies → aws-node · VPC CNI agent → coredns-1 → menu-db-0 → orders-db-0
📄 network-policies/menu-api-egress.yamlyaml
# network-policies/menu-api-egress.yaml — DNS + menu-db only
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: menu-api-egress-network-policy
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which Pods?
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
  # ② Which direction?
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  # ④ Where may they go?
  egress:
    - # DNS to CoreDNS
      to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              k8s-app: kube-dns
      ports:
        - { protocol: UDP, port: 53 }
        - { protocol: TCP, port: 53 }
    - # menu-db only — orders-db is not listed, so it is blocked
      to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: jahez-data
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: menu-db
      ports:
        - { protocol: TCP, port: 5432 }

🌳 NetworkPolicy
① Which Pods?group
podSelectorobjectrequiredPods in this namespace the policy applies to; {} = all
ValueMeaning
{}every Pod in the namespace
matchLabels: {app: menu-api}only menu-api Pods
② Which directions?group
policyTypeslistIngress, Egress or both — listed directions become deny-by-default
⚠ Watch out

Omitted → Ingress only (plus Egress if an egress section exists).

③ Who may come in?group
ingress[].from[]listpeers allowed to connect
• podSelectorobjectPods (same namespace unless combined)
• namespaceSelectorobjectnamespaces by label
• ipBlockobjectcidr + except
• ingress[].ports[]listprotocol + port (Pod port, not Service port)
④ Where may they go?group
• egress[].to[]listdestinations (same peer types)
• egress[].ports[]listprotocol + port (+ endPort for ranges)
Enforcement on EKS

The VPC CNI enforces NetworkPolicy only with the network-policy agent on: EKS add-on configuration {"enableNetworkPolicy": "true"}. Without it (or with flannel) the objects are accepted and do nothing.

7.1Default deny

In one sentence

An empty podSelector with both policyTypes locks every Pod in the namespace until other policies open specific paths.

📄 network-policies/default-deny.yamlyaml
# network-policies/default-deny.yaml — nothing in, nothing out, until allowed
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-network-policy
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which Pods?  (empty = every Pod in jahez-prod)
  podSelector: {}
  # ② Which directions are locked?
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress
    - Egress

Applying default-deny alone cuts DNS and the controller → app path at once: every request returns 504. Ship it in the same commit as the allow policies.

7.2Allow the controller in

In one sentence

Only ingress-nginx Pods may open the app port; everything else in the cluster is still denied.

⎈ Full cluster · After Ingress — one NLB, ingress-nginx Pods route by host + path
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen
Lit: ingress-nginx controller Pods → menu-api Pods → orders-api Pods
📄 network-policies/allow-ingress-nginx.yamlyaml
# network-policies/allow-ingress-nginx.yaml — only the controller may call the apps
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-ingress-nginx-network-policy
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which Pods?
  podSelector:
    matchExpressions:
      - key: app
        operator: In
        values: [menu-api, orders-api]
  # ② Which direction?
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress
  # ③ Who may come in?
  ingress:
    - from:
        - namespaceSelector:              # AND: same list item
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: ingress-nginx
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app.kubernetes.io/name: ingress-nginx
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080

📄 network-policies/orders-api-egress.yamlyaml
# network-policies/orders-api-egress.yaml — DNS + orders-db + Redis + payment gateway
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: orders-api-egress-network-policy
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: orders-api
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              k8s-app: kube-dns
      ports:
        - { protocol: UDP, port: 53 }
        - { protocol: TCP, port: 53 }
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: jahez-data
          podSelector:
            matchExpressions:
              - key: app
                operator: In
                values: [orders-db, redis]
      ports:
        - { protocol: TCP, port: 5432 }
        - { protocol: TCP, port: 6379 }
    - # payment gateway — outside the cluster, by CIDR
      to:
        - ipBlock:
            cidr: 203.0.113.0/24
      ports:
        - { protocol: TCP, port: 443 }

7.4Selectors: AND vs OR

In one sentence

Selectors in one list item are combined with AND; separate list items are OR — one dash changes who gets in.

YAML shapeMeaning
from:
  - namespaceSelector: {…}
    podSelector: {…}
AND — Pods with this label in namespaces with that label (one list item)
from:
  - namespaceSelector: {…}
  - podSelector: {…}
OR — any Pod in those namespaces, or those Pods in this namespace (two items)
⚠ The one-dash difference

A stray - before podSelector turns AND into OR and silently opens the app to every Pod in ingress-nginx-labelled namespaces — or to every Pod in its own namespace.

7.5Fixed egress IPs and egress gateways

In one sentence

NetworkPolicy only allows or drops; a fixed outbound IP comes from the NAT Gateway (or an egress gateway), not from Kubernetes objects.

⎈ Full cluster · After Ingress — one NLB, ingress-nginx Pods route by host + path
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen
Lit: orders-api Pods → NetworkPolicies → NAT Gateway → Payment gateway

NetworkPolicy decides whether a packet may leave. The source IP seen outside comes from the VPC: private-subnet nodes leave through a NAT Gateway with a fixed Elastic IP — give that IP to partners. For per-namespace egress IPs or DNS-name allow-lists use an egress gateway (Cilium / Istio) or Calico/Cilium DNS policies.

8.1kubectl create ingress

⌘ kubectl create ingress
In one sentence

Builds an Ingress from flags — the fastest way in CKAD and a quick way to generate YAML for git.

⎈ Full cluster · After Ingress — one NLB, ingress-nginx Pods route by host + path
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen
Lit: kubectl · helm
kubectl create ingress api-ingress --class=nginx \
  --rule="api.jahez.net/menu*=menu-api-service:80,tls=api-jahez-net-tls-secret" \
  --rule="api.jahez.net/orders*=orders-api-service:80" \
  -n jahez-prod --dry-run=client -o yaml
💡 Command hint
build the object→send to API server→create it

Builds an Ingress from flags — the fastest way in CKAD and a quick way to generate YAML for git.

kubectl create ingressthe command
api-ingressobject name or argument
--class=nginxIngressClass name
▤ example outputoutput
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: api-ingress
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
  - host: api.jahez.net
    http:
      paths:
      - backend:
          service:
            name: menu-api-service
            port:
              number: 80
        path: /menu
        pathType: Prefix
      - backend:
          service:
            name: orders-api-service
            port:
              number: 80
        path: /orders
        pathType: Prefix
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - api.jahez.net
    secretName: api-jahez-net-tls-secret
status:
  loadBalancer: {}
Result
YAML ready to save as ingress/api-ingress.yaml.
✕ When it fails
  • /menu without * → Exact, not Prefix (the most common exam mistake).
  • Backend in another namespace cannot be expressed — the Service must be local.
Template
template
!kubectl create ingress! <NAME> [--class=<CLASS>]
  --rule="<HOST>/<PATH>[*]=<SERVICE>:<PORT>[,tls[=<SECRET>]]" [--rule=…]
  [--default-backend=<SERVICE>:<PORT>] [--annotation=<KEY>=<VALUE>]
  [-n <NAMESPACE>] [--dry-run=client -o yaml]
Parameters
ParameterMeaningSample valuesExample
NAMErequiredIngress nameapi-ingress
backoffice-ingress		kubectl create ingress backoffice-ingress --rule="backoffice.jahez.net/*=menu-api-service:80" -n jahez-prod
--rulerequiredhost/path=service:port; trailing * = Prefix; ,tls adds TLSapi.jahez.net/menu*=menu-api-service:80
api.jahez.net/menu/health=menu-api-service:80
/*=menu-api-service:80
api.jahez.net/*=menu-api-service:http,tls=api-jahez-net-tls-secret		kubectl create ingress path-ingress --rule="api.jahez.net/menu*=menu-api-service:80" -n jahez-prod
--classIngressClassnginx
alb		kubectl create ingress class-ingress --class=nginx --rule="t.jahez.net/*=menu-api-service:80" -n jahez-prod
--default-backendservice:port for unmatched requestsmenu-api-service:80kubectl create ingress catch-ingress --class=nginx --default-backend=menu-api-service:80 -n jahez-prod
--annotationadd one annotation (repeatable)nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect=true
cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer=letsencrypt-prod-cluster-issuer		kubectl create ingress tls-ingress --class=nginx --rule="api.jahez.net/*=menu-api-service:80,tls" --annotation=cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer=letsencrypt-prod-cluster-issuer -n jahez-prod
-nnamespacejahez-prodkubectl create ingress ns-ingress --rule="t.jahez.net/*=menu-api-service:80" -n jahez-prod
--dry-run=client -o yamlprint YAML, send nothingclientkubectl create ingress y-ingress --rule="t.jahez.net/*=menu-api-service:80" --dry-run=client -o yaml
Watch out
  • Quote every --rule (the * is a shell glob).
  • tls without =SECRET uses no secretName → only works with cert-manager / default cert.
  • Generates no annotations unless you pass --annotation.

NAMEkubectl create ingress backoffice-ingress --rule="backoffice.jahez.net/*=menu-api-service:80" -n jahez-prodsmallest valid Ingress
--rule (Prefix)kubectl create ingress p-ingress --rule="api.jahez.net/menu*=menu-api-service:80" -n jahez-prod* → pathType Prefix
--rule (Exact)kubectl create ingress e-ingress --rule="api.jahez.net/menu/health=menu-api-service:80" -n jahez-prodno * → Exact
--rule (no host)kubectl create ingress any-ingress --rule="/*=menu-api-service:80" -n jahez-prodmatches every host
--rule (tls)kubectl create ingress t-ingress --rule="api.jahez.net/*=menu-api-service:80,tls=api-jahez-net-tls-secret" -n jahez-prodadds spec.tls
--classkubectl create ingress c-ingress --class=nginx --rule="t.jahez.net/*=menu-api-service:80" -n jahez-prodsets ingressClassName
--default-backendkubectl create ingress d-ingress --class=nginx --default-backend=menu-api-service:80 -n jahez-prodcatch-all only
--annotationkubectl create ingress a-ingress --class=nginx --rule="t.jahez.net/*=menu-api-service:80" --annotation=nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps=100 -n jahez-prodannotation in metadata
-nkubectl create ingress n-ingress --rule="t.jahez.net/*=menu-api-service:80" -n jahez-prodnamespace
--dry-run=client -o yamlkubectl create ingress y-ingress --rule="t.jahez.net/*=menu-api-service:80" --dry-run=client -o yaml > ingress/y-ingress.yamlsave YAML for git

8.2kubectl apply -f

⌘ kubectl apply -f
In one sentence

Sends the files to the API server, which creates or updates each object; the controller then reloads its routes.

⎈ Full cluster · After Ingress — one NLB, ingress-nginx Pods route by host + path
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen
Lit: Ingress ×5 → kubectl · helm → kube-apiserver → ingress-nginx controller Pods
kubectl apply -f ingress/
💡 Command hint
read the file→send to API server→create / update objects→controller reacts

Sends the files to the API server, which creates or updates each object; the controller then reloads its routes.

kubectl applythe command
-f ingress/file, folder or URL
▤ example outputoutput
ingress.networking.k8s.io/api-ingress unchanged
ingress.networking.k8s.io/legacy-rewrite-ingress unchanged
ingress.networking.k8s.io/orders-canary-ingress configured

ingress.networking.k8s.io/subdomains-ingress unchanged
Result
objects stored; controller reloads within seconds.
✕ When it fails
  • webhook denied: admission webhook "validate.nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io" denied the request: host "api.jahez.net" and path "/menu" is already defined in ingress jahez-prod/api-ingress.
  • Service not found is not an apply error — check describe afterwards.
Template
template
!kubectl apply! -f <FILE|FOLDER|URL> [-n <NAMESPACE>] [--dry-run=server] [--server-side] [-R]
Parameters
ParameterMeaningSample valuesExample
-frequiredfile, folder or URLingress/api-ingress.yaml
ingress/
-		kubectl apply -f ingress/api-ingress.yaml
-nnamespace if the file has nonejahez-prodkubectl apply -f ingress/ -n jahez-prod
--dry-run=serverrun validation + webhook, save nothingserverkubectl apply -f ingress/api-ingress.yaml --dry-run=server
--server-sideserver-side apply with field ownershiptruekubectl apply -f ingress/ --server-side
-Rrecurse into sub-folderstruekubectl apply -R -f network-policies/
Watch out
  • Always kubectl diff -f in PRs.
  • Annotations removed from the file are removed from the object (3-way merge) — good; but changes made with kubectl annotate are overwritten on the next apply.

-nkubectl apply -f ingress/ -n jahez-proddefault namespace
--dry-run=serverkubectl apply -f ingress/api-ingress.yaml --dry-run=serverwebhook check only
--server-sidekubectl apply -f ingress/ --server-sideSSA
-Rkubectl apply -R -f network-policies/recursive

kubectl apply -f ingress/ --dry-run=server

CKAD labs

9.1Labs 1–3 · create, fix, secure

LAB 1Path fan-out, imperatively

In namespace jahez-prod, Services menu-api-service:80 and orders-api-service:80 exist. Create Ingress api-ingress with class nginx: host api.jahez.net, /menu and everything below to menu-api, /orders and below to orders-api.

What you will build
⎈ Full cluster · After Ingress — one NLB, ingress-nginx Pods route by host + path
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen
Lit: Customer app → menu-api-service → orders-api-service
Show solution
⌘ commandsbash
kubectl create ingress api-ingress -n jahez-prod --class=nginx \
  --rule="api.jahez.net/menu*=menu-api-service:80" \
  --rule="api.jahez.net/orders*=orders-api-service:80"
📄 lab1/api-ingress.yamlyaml
# lab1/api-ingress.yaml — the declarative equivalent
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: api-ingress
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
    - host: api.jahez.net
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /menu
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service: { name: menu-api-service, port: { number: 80 } }
          - path: /orders
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service: { name: orders-api-service, port: { number: 80 } }
Verify
⌘ verifybash
kubectl get ing api-ingress -n jahez-prod -o jsonpath="{.spec.rules[0].http.paths[*].pathType}"
curl -s -H "Host: api.jahez.net" http://$(kubectl get ing api-ingress -n jahez-prod -o jsonpath="{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].hostname}")/orders/health
▤ example outputoutput
Prefix Prefix
Healthy (orders-api 3.8.1)
Exam traps
  • Forgetting * → Exact → /menu/categories returns 404.
  • Forgetting -n → created in default, where the Services do not exist.
LAB 2Fix a broken Ingress

Users get 404 on https://api.jahez.net/menu/categories and 503 on /orders. Fix broken-ingress (below) without deleting it.

What you will build
⎈ Full cluster · After Ingress — one NLB, ingress-nginx Pods route by host + path
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen
Lit: Customer app → Ingress ×5 → menu-api-service → orders-api-service
Show solution
⌘ commandsbash
kubectl describe ing broken-ingress -n jahez-prod          # Backends: <error: endpoints … port 8080>
kubectl get svc orders-api-service -n jahez-prod            # PORT(S) 80/TCP
kubectl edit ing broken-ingress -n jahez-prod               # apply the three fixes below
📄 lab2/broken-ingress.yamlyaml
# lab2/broken-ingress.yaml — fixed version (comments mark the three bugs)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: broken-ingress
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx            # bug 3: was missing → no controller served it
  rules:
    - host: api.jahez.net
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /menu
            pathType: Prefix         # bug 1: was Exact → /menu/categories did not match
            backend:
              service:
                name: menu-api-service
                port: { number: 80 }
          - path: /orders
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: orders-api-service
                port: { number: 80 } # bug 2: was 8080 (the containerPort, not the Service port)
Verify
⌘ verifybash
kubectl get ing broken-ingress -n jahez-prod
for p in menu/categories orders/health; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$p %{http_code}\n" https://api.jahez.net/$p; done
▤ example outputoutput
NAME             CLASS   HOSTS           ADDRESS                                        PORTS   AGE
broken-ingress   nginx   api.jahez.net   k8s-ingressn-….elb.me-central-1.amazonaws.com   80      9m
menu/categories 200
orders/health 200
Exam traps
  • Ingress port = Service port, never the containerPort.
  • 404 = no rule matched; 503 = rule matched but no endpoints.
LAB 3TLS with your own certificate

Create a self-signed certificate for secure.jahez.net, store it as secure-jahez-net-tls-secret, and serve menu-api-service over HTTPS on that host with HTTP → HTTPS redirect.

What you will build
⎈ Full cluster · After Ingress — one NLB, ingress-nginx Pods route by host + path
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen
Lit: TLS Secrets → Ingress ×5
Show solution
⌘ commandsbash
openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 30 -newkey rsa:2048 \
  -keyout secure.key -out secure.crt -subj "/CN=secure.jahez.net" \
  -addext "subjectAltName=DNS:secure.jahez.net"
kubectl create secret tls secure-jahez-net-tls-secret --cert=secure.crt --key=secure.key -n jahez-prod
kubectl create ingress secure-ingress -n jahez-prod --class=nginx \
  --rule="secure.jahez.net/*=menu-api-service:80,tls=secure-jahez-net-tls-secret"
📄 lab3/secure-ingress.yamlyaml
# lab3/secure-ingress.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: secure-ingress
  namespace: jahez-prod
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "true"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts: [secure.jahez.net]
      secretName: secure-jahez-net-tls-secret
  rules:
    - host: secure.jahez.net
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service: { name: menu-api-service, port: { number: 80 } }
Verify
⌘ verifybash
LB=$(kubectl get svc ingress-nginx-controller -n ingress-nginx -o jsonpath="{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].hostname}")
IP=$(dig +short $LB | head -1)
curl -sk --resolve secure.jahez.net:443:$IP https://secure.jahez.net/menu/health -v 2>&1 | grep -E "subject:|HTTP/"
curl -sI --resolve secure.jahez.net:80:$IP http://secure.jahez.net/ | head -1
▤ example outputoutput
*  subject: CN=secure.jahez.net
< HTTP/2 200
HTTP/1.1 308 Permanent Redirect
Exam traps
  • Secret type must be kubernetes.io/tls — kubectl create secret generic will not work.
  • Secret must be in the Ingress namespace.

LAB 5Lock down with NetworkPolicy

In jahez-prod: deny all ingress to every Pod, then allow only Pods from namespace ingress-nginx to reach app=menu-api on TCP 8080. Name them lab-deny-network-policy and lab-allow-nginx-network-policy.

What you will build
⎈ Full cluster · After Ingress — one NLB, ingress-nginx Pods route by host + path
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen
Lit: ingress-nginx controller Pods → menu-api Pods
Show solution

📄 lab5/policies.yamlyaml
# lab5/policies.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: lab-deny-network-policy
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: lab-allow-nginx-network-policy
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: { app: menu-api }
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
    - from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: ingress-nginx
      ports:
        - { protocol: TCP, port: 8080 }
Verify
⌘ verifybash
kubectl run probe --rm -it --restart=Never -n jahez-prod --image=busybox:1.36 -- wget -qO- -T 3 http://menu-api-service/menu/health
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://api.jahez.net/menu/health
▤ example outputoutput
wget: download timed out
pod "probe" deleted
200
Exam traps
  • Allow port 8080 (Pod), not 80 (Service).
  • Use the automatic label kubernetes.io/metadata.name — the namespace may have no other labels.
LAB 6Canary 20 % with a header override

Send 20 % of api.jahez.net/orders to orders-api-canary-service; requests with header X-Canary: always always go to the canary.

What you will build
⎈ Full cluster · After Ingress — one NLB, ingress-nginx Pods route by host + path
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen
Lit: orders-api-canary → Customer app → ingress-nginx controller Pods → orders-api-service
Show solution
⌘ commandsbash
kubectl create ingress lab-canary-ingress -n jahez-prod --class=nginx \
  --rule="api.jahez.net/orders*=orders-api-canary-service:80" \
  --annotation=nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary=true \
  --annotation=nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-weight=20 \
  --annotation=nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-by-header=X-Canary
📄 lab6/lab-canary-ingress.yamlyaml
# lab6/lab-canary-ingress.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: lab-canary-ingress
  namespace: jahez-prod
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary: "true"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-weight: "20"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-by-header: X-Canary
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
    - host: api.jahez.net
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /orders
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service: { name: orders-api-canary-service, port: { number: 80 } }
Verify
⌘ verifybash
for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s https://api.jahez.net/orders/version; echo; done | sort | uniq -c
curl -s -H "X-Canary: always" https://api.jahez.net/orders/version
▤ example outputoutput
     81 3.8.1
     19 3.9.0
3.9.0
Exam traps
  • Host and path must equal the main Ingress exactly.
  • Delete any other canary on the same host + path first (one canary per route).
10

Cheat sheet

10.1One page

⌘ commandsbash
# create
kubectl create ingress NAME --class=nginx \
  --rule="HOST/PATH*=SVC:PORT,tls=SECRET" -n NS
#   PATH*  → Prefix      PATH → Exact
#   /*     → every path  (no host) → every host
kubectl create ingress NAME --default-backend=SVC:PORT
kubectl create secret tls SECRET --cert=c.crt --key=c.key -n NS

# read
kubectl get ing,ingressclass -A
kubectl describe ing NAME -n NS        # rules + endpoints + events
kubectl get ing NAME -n NS -o yaml

# change
kubectl annotate ing NAME KEY="VAL" --overwrite -n NS
kubectl edit ing NAME -n NS
kubectl delete ing NAME -n NS

# debug
kubectl logs -n ingress-nginx deploy/ingress-nginx-controller --tail=50
kubectl get endpointslices -n NS -l kubernetes.io/service-name=SVC
curl -sv --resolve HOST:443:IP https://HOST/PATH
kubectl get certificate,challenge -n NS
📄 Ingress skeletonyaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: x-ingress
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx          # ① controller
  rules:                           # ② host + path
    - host: api.jahez.net
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /menu
            pathType: Prefix       # Exact | Prefix | ImplementationSpecific
            backend:               # ③ Service port (not containerPort)
              service: { name: menu-api-service, port: { number: 80 } }
  tls:                             # ④ TLS Secret, same namespace
    - hosts: [api.jahez.net]
      secretName: api-jahez-net-tls-secret
  defaultBackend:                  # ⑤ no rule matched
    service: { name: menu-api-service, port: { number: 80 } }
Traps
  • 404 nginx page = no rule matched (host, pathType, class).
  • 503 = matched, but the Service has no Ready endpoints or wrong port.
  • 502 = Pod answered badly / wrong protocol; 504 = timeout or NetworkPolicy drop.
  • Fake certificate = TLS Secret missing / wrong namespace / not ready.
  • Annotation values are strings; typos are silently ignored.
  • NetworkPolicy ports are Pod ports; selectors in one item = AND.
  • Default-deny without a DNS egress rule breaks every lookup.
  • ingress-nginx is retired (Mar 2026) — plan Gateway API / another controller.
